label: Bivalence of thought, every proposition is…, from Thought, in affirming or denying, is… and 1 more
meaning: Bridge (#401): the two halves of the thought argument's universal reading, *Metaphysics* IV.7, 1012a2-4, yield bivalence of thought. The formalization's extension of the first half to every proposition (STMT-THOUGHT-AFFIRMS-OR-DENIES-EVERY-PROPOSITION, unattributed) and the sourced second half (STMT-AFFIRMING-OR-DENYING-THOUGHT-IS-TRUE-OR-FALSE) give STMT-EVERY-OBJECT-OF-THOUGHT-JUDGED-TRULY-OR-FALSELY: for every proposition some thought with that object is true or false. No excluded middle is used here; ARIST-MET-1012A-THOUGHT-BIVALENCE-IFF-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE shows the conclusion is equivalent to it given the other readings.
